candidates.changed_node: DIV(TS_MIN($low,21), $close+eps) fused as the new left operand of the reversal-term subtraction
candidates.rationale: Keeps asset_turnover as A's quality gate and B's 21-day price floor (TS_MIN($low,21)), but fuses them into a new ratio: the floor relative to current close, minus A's 5-day mean return. This is a support-distance-conditioned reversal, ranking efficient firms highest when they sit close to their monthly floor and have not already reversed. Neither parent alone has this: A has no price-level context, and B ties the floor to earnings yield rather than a turnover-gated reversal.

candidates.changed_node: MINUS(TS_MEAN($return,10), TS_MEAN($return,5)) replaces A's single-window reversal term
candidates.rationale: Same two parents as pair 1, deliberately fused a different way: drops A's value/floor piece and instead uses its embedded 10-day return window, subtracting B's 5-day return window to build a return term structure (has the stock's very recent drift diverged from its monthly drift), gated by B's turnover rank. Captures quality-conditioned momentum acceleration/deceleration, a horizon-comparison idea present in neither parent's own single-window construction.

candidates.changed_node: TS_CORR(TS_MEAN($return,5), $high-$low, 10) replaces A's reversal wrapper and B's static ratio
candidates.rationale: Keeps A's 5-day mean return and B's high-low range, but instead of A's raw unscaled reversal or B's static shadow ratio, correlates the two over 10 days: does the recent return trend co-move with the daily trading range, gated by A's turnover rank. That is a volatility-clustering-direction signal neither parent captures, since A never looks at range and B's range measure never touches price change.

candidates.changed_node: PLUS(MINUS($high, TS_MIN($low,21)), eps) replaces B's TS_STD-based denominator
candidates.rationale: Keeps B's intraday shadow ($high - $close) and repurposes A's 21-day-low reference level, not its EPS field, as a new denominator: the shadow scaled by how far today's high sits above the monthly low, instead of B's own realized-range normalizer. Captures rejection-from-highs relative to the stock's recent floor-to-ceiling room, a value-context-conditioned reversal-pressure measure absent from either parent's own normalizer. This uses A's price-floor sub-structure only: the full EPS/floor ratio is a 7-node block and cannot be reused without restating A outright.

candidates.changed_node: TS_CORR($high-$close, $return, 21) replaces B's static shadow/range ratio
candidates.rationale: Fuses B's ROA quality screen with A's intraday shadow, correlated against 21-day return rather than statically ratio'd: does a profitable firm's daily rejection-from-highs trend with its own recent performance, an exhaustion-at-the-top signature among quality names that neither parent expresses. Mechanical caveat: RANK($roa) is a 2-node tree (verified via ast_tools.size), so no child can ever share 3+ nodes with B, the crossover gate's own min_crossover_shared floor. This child donates B in full (2 nodes, the maximum possible) plus a genuine 3+-node fragment from A; as literally specified it will still fail crossover_uses_both_parents against B. Recommend exempting single-field atomic parents from the 3-node floor, or growing $roa via MUTATE before offering it to CROSSOVER.

candidates.changed_node: MINUS(TS_MEAN($return,21), TS_MEAN($return,5)) replaces B's rank-spread with a return term structure
candidates.rationale: Fuses A's profitability screen with B's embedded 21-day return window, not its $roe field (B's full rank-spread is a 7-node block and cannot be reused without restating B), subtracting a fresh 5-day return mean to build a return term structure gated by ROA. Same mechanical caveat as pair 5: RANK($roa) is a 2-node tree, so no child can share >=3 nodes with A. This child donates A in full plus a genuine 3+-node fragment from B; it will still fail crossover_uses_both_parents against A as literally specified.

candidates.changed_node: MINUS(CS_ZSCORE($roe), CS_ZSCORE(TS_MEAN($return,21))) replaces A's CS_RANK spread
candidates.rationale: Keeps A's ROE-vs-momentum idea and B's liquidity level, but re-standardizes each side with CS_ZSCORE instead of A's own CS_RANK (which would otherwise restate A's exact 4-node rank-spread verbatim) before ranking the spread and multiplying by B's dollar-volume rank. Asks whether the quality-net-of-momentum edge concentrates in the most liquid, tradable names, a liquidity interaction neither parent expresses alone.

candidates.changed_node: DIV($close, TS_MAX($high,21)+eps) replaces B's min-max stochastic normalization
candidates.rationale: Keeps A's liquidity level and B's 21-day high reference, but replaces B's full min-max stochastic normalization with a simpler close-to-high proximity ratio (avoiding a restatement of B's own denominator) and gates it by a fresh liquidity rank. A volume-confirms-the-breakout interaction: is proximity to the monthly high more meaningful when trading is elevated, something neither a static liquidity level nor an ungated stochastic position expresses.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: CROSSOVER. Each pair below holds two parents from DIFFERENT archive
niches. Return one child per pair that genuinely combines them.

A child must keep a complete sub-expression of at least 3 nodes
from EACH parent, checked mechanically; a child that is really just one parent
with cosmetic changes is rejected. Put both parent ids in `parent_ids`.

neither parent captures alone? A conditioning variable, a normaliser, an
interaction. If you cannot name one, the pair is a bad cross and you should say
so in the rationale rather than force it.
